title: The $357 Cold Email Stack: Offer, List, Copy, Then Tools
description: What a 1,000-a-day cold email setup really costs each month, line by line, and the 4-step order that matters more than any tool.
lead: This is the full guide from the reel. You get the line-by-line math behind the $357 a month, and the order to fix things in: offer, list, copy, then tools.
insider: When a new client comes to us, the tools are the last thing we talk about. A clear offer, a clean list and short emails are how one client got **4,372 replies and 1,061 interested leads in one quarter**. Buying the stack takes an afternoon. Running it every week, with fresh lists and fast replies, is the part we do for clients.

blocks.text: The short answer

A setup that sends **about 1,000 cold emails a day** costs about **$357 a month** in tools. That money buys inboxes, domains and a sending tool. It does not buy replies. Replies come from the offer, the list and the copy. Fix those first.
Where the $357 comes from

We used the numbers from our sending calculator: about 30 emails a day per inbox and 3 inboxes per domain. For 1,000 a day that is **34 inboxes on 12 domains**. Prices below are from the official pricing pages, checked on November 21, 2026. Prices: [Google Workspace](https://workspace.google.com/pricing) Business Starter is $7 per user a month on the annual plan. [Instantly](https://instantly.ai/pricing) Hypergrowth is $107 a month billed monthly. Domain prices vary by registrar, so check yours.

items: **Why Hypergrowth, not Growth?** 1,000 a day is about 22,000 emails in a month of weekdays. Instantly's Growth plan allows 5,000 emails a month. Hypergrowth allows 125,000.
**Paying yearly is cheaper.** Instantly lists Hypergrowth at $85.58 a month on annual billing.
**Lists are not in the $357.** You can start with free sources and your own research. Paid data tools add to the bill.

blocks.text: Why more tools rarely fix zero replies

Every tool on that list does one job: get the email into the inbox. If the email lands and nobody answers, a new tool changes nothing. The reader still sees the same offer, sent to the same people, in the same words.
A tool can't write what you offer.
The 4-step order
Step 1: The offer
**Why it matters:** the offer is the reason to say yes. If a stranger can't see what they get and why it's low risk, nothing else saves the email.

items: Write what you do in one line: "We help [who] get [result] in [time]."
Add one piece of proof: a number, a client type or a short result.
Make the ask small: a 15-minute call, a free audit or a short sample.
Test it: read it out loud. If a friend in that job wouldn't say "yes, send it", rewrite it.

blocks.text: Step 2: The list
**Why it matters:** the best email fails if it goes to people who can't buy. In the reel, 10 names became 4 after we removed people with no budget, no need or the wrong job title.

items: Write down who signs the check: job title, company size, industry, country.
Remove anyone who doesn't match, even if it makes the list smaller.
Verify every email before you send.
Keep your best 2 or 3 reasons why this company needs you now (hiring, new funding, new location).

blocks.text: Step 3: The copy
**Why it matters:** busy people decide in a few seconds. Short, plain emails with one ask are easy to answer.

items: One simple ask at the end.
No images, no attachments, no links in the first email.

blocks.text: Step 4: The tools
**Why last:** tools make a working campaign bigger. They can't make a broken one work. Once steps 1 to 3 get replies on a small test, buy the inboxes you need to scale.

blocks.text: Copy-paste prompt: test your offer before you buy anything

blocks.label: Offer test prompt
blocks.text:
I sell [what you sell] to [who you sell to]. My current cold email offer is:
[paste your offer]

Act as a busy [job title] who gets 50 cold emails a week.
1) In one sentence, tell me what you think I'm offering.
2) Give me 3 reasons you would ignore it.
3) Rewrite the offer in under 25 words with one proof point and one small ask.
4) Give me 2 more versions with a different small ask (audit, sample, 15-minute call).

faq.q: Can I start for less than $357?
faq.a: Yes. That number is for about 1,000 emails a day. A small test with a few inboxes on one or two domains costs much less. Start small, prove the offer, then grow.
Any well-known sending tool with warm-up works. The tool matters far less than your offer, list and copy.

faq.q: How do I know if my problem is the offer or the list?
faq.a: Read your replies. "Not interested" from the right people points to the offer. "Wrong person" or "we don't do that" points to the list.
